title: 고등법원 부의 지방법원 소재지에서의 사무처리에 관한 규칙 / queue:ARTICLE:4:0:00004:part:1/1
title_original: 고등법원 부의 지방법원 소재지에서의 사무처리에 관한 규칙
full_text:
Article 4 (Scope of Adjudicative Affairs)
(1) An outlying division of a High Court shall adjudicate the following cases among those over which a High Court has jurisdiction under Article 28 of the Court Organization Act: <Amended on February 20, 2008; December 13, 2010>
1. Appeals against first-instance judgments of the District Court located at the seat of the outlying division or branches under its jurisdiction;
2. Appeals against first-instance rulings, decisions, or orders of the relevant District Court or branch;
3. Cases falling under the jurisdiction of a High Court under other statutes where the ordinary venue of the defendant, respondent, or opposing party is within the jurisdiction of the relevant District Court or branch.
(2) Where necessary in light of the nature, expertise, complexity, value of the subject matter, etc. of a case, the President of the High Court may, with permission of the Chief Justice, determine that part of the adjudicative affairs under paragraph (1) shall be handled by the High Court.
(3) At the request of the presiding judge, the President of the High Court may have a case filed with an outlying division tried by the High Court where appropriate, or a case filed with the High Court tried by the outlying division where appropriate. <Newly Inserted on February 20, 2008>
